diffs.diff: pin count: part has 18 (5V GND EN1 EN2 CS1 CS2 INA2 PWM1 PWM2 INA1 INB1 INB2 VIN PGND OUTA1 OUTB1 OUTA2 OUTB2), datasheet reading has 12 (5V GND A2 A3 D0 D1 D4 D5 D6 D7 D8 D9)
diffs.evidence: The second reading took the sketch's 'const int enPin[2] = {0, 1};' as D0/D1, but on this shield layout (SparkFun MonsterMoto-Shield-v12 schematic: EN1->A0, EN2->A1, CS1->A2, CS2->A3) the enables are analog pins, as the same-layout shield's vendor page states 'A0 = EN/DIAG 1 A1 = EN/DIAG 2'; the second reading also omitted the VIN/- power terminal and the four motor screw terminals, which the model includes as VIN, PGND, OUTA1/OUTB1/OUTA2/OUTB2.

diffs.diff: minimum supply: part 4.5 V, datasheet reading 5.5 V
diffs.evidence: The 5.5 V figure is the VNH2SP30-E battery (motor) supply, 'Shuts down the device outside the range [5.5V..16V] for the battery voltage', which the model already applies to its VIN pin (supply vmin 5.5, vmax 16); the part-level 4.5-5.5 V range is the Arduino 5V header that only feeds the 4.7 kOhm EN pull-ups, not the chip's VCC.
